newsitem.title: UK: London gold price range-bound, silver seen upwardly mobile.
newsitem.headline: London gold price range-bound, silver seen upwardly mobile.

text.p: Gold prices were wedged in a tight range on Thursday and seen likely to remain so, while silver and platinum were stronger following overnight gains.
"Gold is very steady, it seems to be range trapped with not much potential outside $379-$382," a London-based dealer said.
Bullion closed at $381.95 an ounce, compared with $381.35 on Wednesday afternoon.
Selling at around $382 from speculators and gold producers capped rises. On the downside there was firm support but gold ignored the white metals' strength, dealers said.
"Gold is running into selling at around $382. There's not a lot it can do at this point," a dealer said.
Silver, however, was decidedly stronger closing at $5.01 an ounce, up seven cents from Wednesday's London close.
It surged some 10 cents on Wednesday in a rally led by U.S. investment funds and closed near the day's highs in New York.
"Silver closed impressively, breaking the downtrend," a dealer said.
But it struggled at the key $5 level, below which it has traded for three weeks. A layer of selling around $4.98-$4.99 blocked its rise most of the day, dealers said.
"The close lends a bullish sentiment to the market. Silver should have a look at $5, and a break on the upside would target $5.04-$5.05," a dealer said.
Interest in silver was primarily speculative, boosted by reports in recent days of declining warehouse stocks.
Stocks in New York's Comex futures market stocks set a fresh low for the year on Wednesday.
"There was some fresh buying in silver, and the market was short so it ran some stops (triggered buying at pre-set price levels) yesterday (Wednesday)," a dealer said.
Platinum also performed well, indicated up $3.75 from Wednesday's London close at $388.75. Silver's gains provided an additional boost to already rising prices.
Platinum had been due for an upside correction, with $390 an ounce as the target, after sliding to near three-year lows in recent weeks, analysts said.
Palladium was up $1.25 at $118.25. But it was vulnerable since slipping again below the key $120 level on Monday.
